={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens: 1024, thinking: { type: "disabled" }, messages: [{ role: "user", content: "You are picking a topic for a YouTube Shorts video.

CRITERIA: pick whatever topic the majority of people would genuinely stop scrolling for - your own judgment, no fixed category, format, or pattern list to pick from.

FORMAT IS OPEN: a topic can be a fact, hypothetical, scale question, or comparison - e.g. "How would spending 1 trillion dollars actually look?" is as valid as a straightforward fact. The only requirement: the answer must be groundable in real math or information, never fabricated. Vary the shape freely.

REJECT trivia that only becomes interesting after the explanation - stated plainly, the topic itself must already create real curiosity, not just the payoff behind it.

VARY THE SHAPE, NOT JUST THE SUBJECT: check the already-used topics below for their STRUCTURE, not just their subject - e.g. "what if everyone did X at once" is one shape; "a hidden mechanism inside something ordinary" is another, which a car-safety fact and a body-biology fact could both share despite being different subjects. If recent entries cluster on one shape, pick a genuinely different one.

HARD EXCLUSION (non-negotiable): never a medical or health topic - no diseases, symptoms, treatments, medications, procedures, even framed as a surprising fact.

Must NOT closely resemble any of these already-used topics: " + JSON.stringify($('Ensure Topics Array').item.json.topics.map(t => t.topic)) + " - Output ONLY the topic as one plain sentence. No quotes, no JSON, no markdown, no preamble, no category label." }] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "claude-opus-4-8", max_tokens: 8192, messages: [{ role: "user", content: "You are the head writer for a YouTube Shorts channel built for maximum virality and watch time with a broad audience.

HARD EXCLUSION (non-negotiable): never write about medical or health topics - no diseases, conditions, symptoms, treatments, medications, surgeries, or medical procedures, even framed as a surprising fact. If the given topic drifts toward this, reframe it toward a genuinely non-medical angle instead.

IMPORTANT: There is NO fixed topic restriction, and NO forced format. You are given a topic and you develop the best version of it - which might be a surprise/curiosity-gap fact, or might be a straightforward explainer, how-to, comparison, or story. Do not force every topic into a clickbait mold.

AUDIENCE: Broad, general audience. They want either a concrete surprising fact OR a genuinely clear, useful explanation - no vague generalities, no lifestyle-influencer fluff.

VOICE: Confident, direct, to the point - but also genuinely warm and funny, like a smart friend telling you something wild over drinks, not a narrator reading facts at you. React to your own story: a dry aside, a wry comparison, mild disbelief at the thing you are describing. Humor should come from the material itself (an absurd detail, an ironic twist, a comparison that makes the scale click) - never a forced joke bolted on. If a line could have been written by a textbook, rewrite it until it sounds like a person actually reacting to the story as they tell it.

HOOK - the single most important sentence in the video. Everything below serves ONE goal: a hook that sounds like a genuinely charming, funny, sharp person just said something wild - not a checklist being satisfied. If a hook technically passes every rule below but reads flat or generic, it has failed the actual goal. Rewrite for charm first, then verify it against the rules.\n\nTHE CORE MECHANIC - withhold, don\u2019t resolve: for surprise/secret/contradiction topics, state the contradiction or secret but never the number or mechanism - that\u2019s the payoff, saved for inside the video. On this channel, hooks that led with a statistic averaged 84 views; hooks that withheld it averaged 298 - 3.5x more. For genuine explainers/how-tos, this rule does not apply - state the value directly and specifically instead.\n- WEAK (real underperformer): World\u2019s Longest Flight Burns 161,000 Litres of Fuel -> STRONG: The world\u2019s longest flight burns more fuel than you will use in your entire life.\n- WEAK: Sleep is important for your brain. -> STRONG: Your brain deletes memories on purpose every single night.\nWhat makes STRONG work: a SPECIFIC named entity doing something UNEXPECTED, stated flatly and confidently - never hedged.\n\nDELIVERY - direct, personal, and genuinely funny: address the viewer directly and physically (your eyes, your hand, your brain, right now) and let the sentence carry real ominous or awe-struck energy - dread and awe are assets. Vary the actual grammatical shape every time - do not default to the same "Right now, your X..." template repeatedly. Some options, not a checklist to rotate through: a flat impossible-sounding statement, a direct command, a contradiction stated as plain fact, a question that answers itself uncomfortably. The only banned openers are dead filler that adds no drama: \u201chave you ever\u201d, \u201clet\u2019s explore\u201d, \u201cin today\u2019s video\u201d, \u201cit\u2019s important to\u201d, \u201cthe truth is\u201d, \u201cbasically\u201d, \u201chonestly\u201d. \u201cDid you know\u201d, \u201cimagine\u201d, \u201cpicture\u201d, and \u201clook at\u201d are genuinely fine when they lead into something sharp - the problem was never the opener, it\u2019s vague or generic delivery. Generic hype words are also banned regardless of framing: crazy, insane, unbelievable, shocking, mind-blowing, impossible, wild.\n\nFIVE DIFFERENT HOOKS, FIVE DIFFERENT SHAPES: draft five real candidates, each genuinely different in structure and angle - not five phrasings of the same idea. Score each on: does it withhold the payoff (where that rule applies)? does it name something specific and concrete? would a stranger react with real surprise or genuine want-to-know, not a shrug? Output all five in hook_candidates, the strongest in hook.\n\nHONEST CLICKBAIT: withhold or promise, never exaggerate or invent. Every claim must be fully paid off by the script - overpromising tanks retention, which is worse than a plain hook.\n\nPLAN THE ENDING FIRST: before writing any scene, decide the hook, the kicker, and the closing call-to-action together as one unit. The kicker is the payoff plus a line that reframes or tops it; the CTA immediately follows as one natural spoken sentence - a specific, genuine question about THIS fact that invites a real answer (e.g. built around a real choice, a personal reaction, or a detail only the viewer would know) - never a generic "comment below" or "what do you think" filler. Everything before this exists only to earn that final moment.\n\nSTRUCTURE - pick whichever fits the topic, do not force curiosity-gap structure onto an explainer:
- OPEN LOOP / ESCALATE / PAY OFF (surprise, secret, or contradiction topics): scene 1 = hook only, middle scene(s) escalate without revealing the payoff, final scene delivers the answer plus a kicker.
- CLEAR EXPLAINER (how-tos, mechanisms, straightforward informative topics): scene 1 = state plainly what this explains, middle scene(s) walk through the key steps or reasons in order, final scene lands the most useful or memorable takeaway. No need to withhold anything - clarity beats suspense here.
Either way: every transition must carry BUT or THEREFORE tension, never AND THEN listing - if a scene could be cut without breaking the chain, it is padding, cut it. End on the strongest line - no summary, no generic outro - but the final spoken sentence must be a natural, specific call-to-action tied directly to this exact fact (a genuine question inviting a real answer, not "comment below" or "what do you think"). It should read as the natural next thought after the kicker, not a bolted-on afterthought.

SUSTAINED STORYTELLING (critical - this is where scripts most often fail): the hook is not the only place that needs personality and tension. Every middle scene must ALSO read like a person telling a story that keeps getting more interesting, not a list of facts about the same topic. Concretely: each scene should make the previous one MORE surprising in hindsight, add a reaction or a stake, or set up a question the next scene answers - never just "and here is another fact about X." If you could shuffle the middle scenes into a different order without losing anything, they are not actually building a story - rewrite so each one depends on the one before it.

LENGTH TARGET (tightened based on this channel's own real retention data - best performers hold 59-65%, worst hold 30-32% and skew longer): aim for 70-90 total narration words across all scenes - that lands the video around 20-25 seconds, including the closing CTA sentence. 100 words is a HARD ceiling. 3-4 scenes, roughly 18-25 words each. No padding, no repeating a point in different words - every sentence must be load-bearing.

SENTENCE RHYTHM: short, punchy. Avoid semicolons and long subordinate clauses - this is spoken aloud, not read.

VISUAL STYLE - PROFESSIONAL HOUSE STYLE (critical): this channel uses Pexels stock video and photos exclusively (NO AI image generation). The stock_search_query field drives all visual selection.

STOCK SEARCH QUERIES - RULES:
- stock_search_query: 2-4 plain concrete nouns describing the literal subject and setting, written for a stock-video/photo search engine (e.g. "woman grocery shopping", "honey jar closeup", "rocket launch"). Must NOT include style/lighting/camera language.
- Think about what Pexels would actually have footage of. Prefer concrete, filmable subjects over abstract concepts.
- SCENE 1 IS THE THUMBNAIL: its visual is the first frame in the feed. The stock_search_query for scene 1 should target the most visually striking, recognizable image of the subject.
- Each scene's stock_search_query must be SPECIFIC and ACCURATE to that scene's exact beat - no generic filler.

COMMENT MECHANIC (critical for engagement): in comment_hook, give a short, concrete question or mildly interesting opinion tied directly to THIS content (e.g. Would you have guessed the shrimp? or Which step do you already do?). NOT part of the narration - it appears as on-screen text in the final 1-2 seconds. Never a generic line like what do you think.

SELF-REVIEW before output (silent): Did you plan the hook AND kicker first? Did you pick the hook pattern and structure that genuinely fits this topic, rather than forcing curiosity-gap onto an explainer or vice versa? Do all transitions carry BUT/THEREFORE tension? Does the narration end on the kicker followed immediately by one specific, non-generic spoken CTA question? Total narration 70-90 words? Every stock_search_query specific to its beat? Rewrite anything that fails. Then output ONLY the final result.

SEO/TAGS STRATEGY:
- title: for surprise topics, withhold the why/how/figure - never include the payoff number (this channel’s data: number-led titles average 3.5x fewer views). For explainers, state the value clearly and specifically. Prefer recurring template families the channel can repeat and compound on. Strong keyword early where natural. MAXIMUM 50 characters (mobile screens truncate longer titles - this is a hard ceiling, not a target to approach).
- tags: mix broad viral tags (fun facts, how to, shorts, explained) with specific tags for this exact topic.
- seo_description: first 1-2 sentences carry the key search terms, then end with a comment-inviting question.

VISUAL SOURCE PER SCENE - stock photo OR animated template:
For each scene, decide whether a real stock photo or a designed animated template better serves that specific beat. Templates give exact, designed visuals for beats that are fundamentally about a NUMBER, a COMPARISON, or a PUNCHY LINE - things no stock photo can show precisely. Use a template when the beat IS one of these three shapes; use stock otherwise.

AVAILABLE TEMPLATES (use the exact name and exact data fields shown):
1. "stat_reveal" - a single striking number/stat as a payoff. data: {statValue: string (the number/figure, short), label: string (what it means, short phrase)}
2. "comparison" - two values side by side. data: {leftLabel: string, leftValue: string, rightLabel: string, rightValue: string}
3. "kinetic_text" - one punchy line revealed word by word. data: {line: string (under 8 words)}

For each scene, output:
- visual_source: "stock" or "template"
- if "template": template_name (one of the three above, exact match) and template_data (the exact fields that template requires, values drawn from this scene's narration)
- if "stock": provide stock_search_query as specified in the rules above
A typical script might use "template" for the scene containing the core number/payoff and "stock" for the rest - do not force every scene into a template, and do not force every scene into stock either.

OUTPUT - valid JSON only, no markdown fences, no preamble, no trailing commas:
{"hook": string, "hook_type": string, "hook_candidates": array of exactly 5 strings, "title": string (MAXIMUM 50 characters), "seo_description": string, "comment_hook": string, "tags": array of 8-15 strings, "full_script": string, "caption_style": "upbeat"|"serious"|"funny"|"neutral", "scenes": [{"scene_index": number, "point": string, "narration": string, "visual_source": "stock"|"template", "stock_search_query": string, "template_name": string, "template_data": object}]}

Topic: " + $json.topic }] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens: 8192, thinking: { type: "disabled" }, messages: [{ role: "user", content: "You are a strict editor for a viral facts/comparison YouTube Shorts channel with a broad general audience. You will be given a draft script as JSON. Find and fix everything that sounds vague, unverifiable, too long, or would require the AI video generator to render readable text - then output the corrected JSON in the exact same schema.

CHECK FOR AND FIX:
0. MEDICAL EXCLUSION: if any scene or the hook/title touches disease, illness, symptoms, treatment, medication, surgery, or any medical/health topic, rewrite that scene entirely toward a non-medical angle - this overrides every other instruction below.
1. Banned filler/hype: have you ever, let’s explore, in today’s video, did you know, it’s important to, the truth is, basically, honestly, crazy, insane, unbelievable, shocking, mind-blowing, impossible, wild, the reason is, this happens because, that’s because. Remove any of these. “Imagine”, “picture”, and “look at” are NOT on this list - they are the encouraged dramatic style, do not remove them.
1. DRAMATIC HOOK STYLE (enforce this, do not soften it): the hook must use direct, imperative address ("Picture X", "Look at your own X", "Right now, your X...") and lead into a bold, high-drama claim - mortality, bodily horror, visceral scale, or danger. "Did you know", "imagine", and similar framing openers are ENCOURAGED here, not banned. If a hook reads flat, neutral, or academic instead of dramatic and personal, rewrite it to match this energy: "Right now, your eyes are lying to you - there's a blind spot in your vision so large a whole face could disappear into it."
2. Vague claims without a concrete number, price, or specific - make every point quotable and specific.
3. Sentences that sound written rather than spoken - rewrite anything stiff, short punchy sentences preferred.
4. HOOK STRENGTH (apply the hardest scrutiny here): a hook can be factually true and still be WEAK if it has no tension or specific stakes. Test it: would a stranger hearing ONLY this sentence react with a specific wait-what, or just shrug? If it starts with any framing like Here's something, Did you know, Most people don't realize, or X is more Y than you think - strip the framing and lead directly with the sharpest specific claim. Rewrite until it names a specific entity doing something concretely unexpected, stated flatly with no hedging.
5. TOTAL WORD COUNT: sum the words across every scene’s narration. If the total exceeds 100 words, cut content - remove repetition, shorten sentences, drop the weakest point entirely if needed. This is a hard requirement.
6. Confirm each stock scene has a stock_search_query that is specific and searchable on Pexels - use concrete nouns for filmable subjects.
8. Confirm the title field is 50 characters or fewer (mobile-screen fit) - if longer, rewrite it tighter rather than truncate mid-word.
9. Confirm tags contains 8-15 relevant, specific terms (no generic filler tags unrelated to the topic) and that seo_description includes the key search terms in the first sentences and ends with a comment-inviting question.
10. Confirm comment_hook is specific to this exact fact (not a generic "what do you think") and stock_search_query on every stock scene is concrete and specific to the beat.

11. HOOK CANDIDATE REVIEW: compare the chosen hook against every entry in hook_candidates. If any candidate scores higher on curiosity gap + specificity, swap it in as the hook. You may also write one new hook combining the strongest elements of multiple candidates - if it beats them all, use it. The final hook must withhold a resolution that the script then clearly delivers.
12. TITLE GAP CHECK: if the title resolves the surprise (gives away the why/how), rewrite it to state the claim but withhold the resolution.

13. FLOW CHECK: every scene transition must carry BUT or THEREFORE tension, never and-then listing - rewrite any flat sequential transition.
14. ENDING CHECK: the narration must stop abruptly on the strongest kicker line. Delete any summary, outro, or spoken call-to-action sentence at the end.
15. LENGTH TARGET: total narration (including the closing CTA sentence) should land between 70 and 90 words - trim if over 100, and if far under 60, check whether the payoff is being rushed.

Output ONLY the corrected JSON, same schema as input, no markdown fences, no preamble, no commentary about what you changed.

Draft to edit:
" + JSON.stringify($json.draft) }] }) }}

const lastErrors = $input.first().json.lastErrors || [];
throw new Error('Script generation failed validation 3 times in a row with fresh topics each time - giving up for this scheduled run rather than posting a bad video. Last errors: ' + lastErrors.join(' | '));

const prevAttempt = $('Init Poll Counter').item.json.pollAttempt ?? 0;
return { json: { jobId: $('Init Poll Counter').item.json.jobId, pollAttempt: prevAttempt + 1 } };
throw new Error('Compose job did not finish within 40 poll attempts (~320s) - job_id: ' + $json.jobId + '. The render may be stuck; check shorts-compose logs directly.');
